step6_output.answer_core: Do not choose a dissertation direction yet. Treat the next few weeks as a short, low‑cost test rather than a commitment. The real decision turns on two gates. First, check whether the Silva direction can actually become a dissertation: confirm you can get early data, identify a collaborator who can compensate for the lab’s single‑cell gaps, and get explicit support from your advisor rather than assuming it. Second, keep the fallback alive while you test Silva. It only remains a fallback if your advisor keeps it resourced, available, and ready for you to re‑enter, and if you set a clear stop date with visible conditions for saying no. Coordinate with your advisor before you involve a committee. Run the Silva probe strictly within the short window you define, and make the continuation decision only after you have actual evidence on both gates.
